review_summary:
This is a static review of the supplied excerpts. I ran nothing and rely on no self-reported test results.

**What holds up**
- The helper reconstructs into an internally owned fresh temp DB, and the signature accepts no caller SQLite or complete flag.
- It requires full coverage and an unchanged bootstrap, approval and trust before any destination write.
- The destination write is one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction of fixed typed rows. It checks the schema and triggers, and it requires receipt, provenance and time facts to be monotonic.
- Durable digest mode fails closed on missing trust, time or interval rows, on an invalid trust status, and on any merge-timestamp mismatch.
- Withdrawn evidence is never labelled `authenticated`.
- The legacy branch and the renderer's authenticated output look unchanged.

**Changes requested**
- `delivery_interval` is overwritten wholesale on every projection. Nothing in the report DB records which interval or coverage the data belongs to, so a narrower projection can later produce a permanent false "evidence MISSING" report. See the first finding.
- Several security-relevant branches have no negative test. These are the destination guards, atomic rollback, rejection of an invalid mode, and byte-exact legacy output. The AC-8 atomicity and legacy-immutability claims are therefore unproven by the committed test. See the second finding.

The test harness is brittle and a connection is not closed; both are minor. Pass is withheld because of the two findings above.

findings.title: delivery_interval is replaced wholesale and is not bound to any interval or coverage, so a narrower rerun permanently mislabels later PRs as MISSING
findings.reason:
The monotonic check at lines 105-106 is skipped for `delivery_trust` and `delivery_interval`. Lines 107-110 then `DELETE` and reinsert the whole table from the current call. `delivery_interval` holds only task ids, so the report DB records neither `interval_end` nor `verified_until`.

Repro path:
1. Run `project_reporting(..., interval_end=E2)`.
2. Run it again with `interval_end=E1 < E2`, for example a retry or an older scheduled call.
3. `delivery_interval` shrinks to the tasks within E1.
4. Durable `Digest.prepare` (factory-digest.py:126) inner-joins `delivery_interval`, so every PR merged in (E1,E2] gets `evidence_status='missing'` even though its receipt, provenance, trust and time rows exist.
5. That batch is confirmed and immutable, and the cursor advances past those PRs, so they are never re-reported with their proof.

This fails closed on authentication, but it is a silent, irreversible loss of evidence in a delivered report. Digest has no way to tell a stale or narrower projection from "no proof exists". A batch for an end the projection never verified is therefore not distinguishable from a verified-empty one, which cuts against AC-7's visible-gap requirement.

Fix: make interval membership monotonic or key it by (interval_end, task). Persist the verified-until value in the report DB. Have durable `prepare` refuse a batch whose `end` exceeds it.

findings.title: Destination guards, atomic rollback, invalid mode and byte-exact legacy output have no tests
findings.reason:
No test exercises the following branches; each is reproducible by inspection of the committed test:
- Helper lines 98, 101 and 106: a pre-existing trigger, a mismatched destination schema, and a conflicting or disappearing existing receipt, provenance or time fact.
- Lines 96-110: a mid-transfer failure leaving the destination byte-identical. The "atomic" claim is only exercised on success and no-op paths.
- The `receipt_mode` validation at factory-digest.py:42. The test sets `view.receipt_mode='durable'` after construction (test line 29), and no test passes an invalid or omitted mode.
- Line 94: the legacy check asserts only that `evidence_status=='authenticated'` and that no `trust_status` key is present. It never compares the canonical legacy payload to a fixed pre-change expectation, so "exact legacy-off output" is not demonstrated for the digest. Only the renderer has an exact-text assertion, at line 11.
- Line 112 covers an already-confirmed batch only. Nothing covers a batch still pending when `receipt_mode` changes.

AC-8's atomic and no-partial-write claims and AC-2's legacy-immutability claim rest on untested code. Add negative cases that snapshot the destination bytes.

findings.title: Test splices another test's source text via string splits and nested exec
findings.reason: Lines 16-18 and 117 read `factory-receipt-coverage-batch.sh`. They split it on the literal markers `"<<'PY'\n"`, `"\ncases=r'''"` and `' assert batch_calls,'`, then `exec` a `repr`-embedded concatenation. Any reformat or edit of that file's markers silently changes or breaks this test: it fails with an unhelpful `IndexError` or `NameError`, or worse, it runs a different fixture. It also makes the dependency on names such as `sources`, `runs`, `PipelineState`, `Runs`, `fixture` and `pipeline` invisible. Share the fixture via a common sourced helper or module, or at least assert the markers exist with clear messages.

findings.title: Destination connection is never closed
findings.reason: `with sqlite3.connect(report) as db:` only commits or rolls back; it does not close the connection. The handle stays open until garbage collection, and the report DB file remains locked or held in long-lived callers. Wrap it in `contextlib.closing`, or close explicitly. `Digest.transaction` in factory-digest.py already closes in `finally`, so this would also match the surrounding idiom.

limitations: Static review of the supplied diff and excerpts only. Nothing was executed, and nothing was verified against T287, T332 or any wiring.

`delivery_trust` is exempt from the immutability check, and the test (lines 97-99) deliberately flips withdrawn back to active when the trust file says active. This is a design choice, not a finding. Withdrawal is not monotonic in the report DB, so rolling back or replacing the local trust file would re-authenticate previously withdrawn proof in future digests. AC-2 says previously reported revoked facts remain annotated, so consider making withdrawal sticky or tying it to a protected trust epoch in a later task.

The helper rows come from its own `reconstruct_interval`, and `coverage()` runs a second, independent reconstruction. Nothing compares the two. Agreement relies on determinism of the frozen `history_head`/`campaign` plus the unchanged-bootstrap check at the end (helper lines 94-95). Coverage could expose a projection digest to bind them.

Real-world report DBs that already hold legacy coordinator `delivery_receipts` or `delivery_provenance` rows (the legacy digest reads those same tables) will be rejected by the schema, `disappears` or conflict guards if they differ from the retained set. This fails closed. Integration behaviour is for T332 and later to confirm.

Pending or uncertain batches are returned unchanged by `prepare` regardless of `receipt_mode` (factory-digest.py:85-87). This is pre-existing and consistent with immutability, but a batch prepared in legacy mode and still undelivered will not pick up durable withdrawn labelling.
The `ReadOnly` wrappers pass `read_blobs` and `read_pull_requests` straight through. Their read-only property depends on the transport implementation, which is not in the supplied excerpts.
`ReadOnly.request` uses a prefix check (`repos/<repo>/`) with no path normalization, the same pattern as the existing archive code. Paths are internally templated here, so no exploit path was shown.
